This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER With the consent, heard finally.
Perused the case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail to the applicant, as he has been arrested on 31.05.2023 in connection with Crime No.242/2022 registered at Police Station Shadora, District Ashoknagar (M.P.) fo r commission of offence punishable under Sections 419, 420,
467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC.

Prosecution case, in brief, is that applicant Shivram Ahirwar S/o Kailash Ahirwar impersonated himself as Shivram Singh S/o Toofan Singh Ahirwar and executed an agreement with regard to the land owned by Shivram Singh S/o Toofan Singh in favour of complainant Manish and took a cheque Shivram Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165241065/
1 bearing No.030062 amounting to Rs.5,00,000/- from him and thereafter deposited the amount in his account.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.
He further submits that as per prosecution case itself co-accused Rajaram prepared forged documents in order to deceive the complainant and fraudulently took away the amount from him.
The applicant is a young boy aged about 30 years and admittedly did not executed the agreement to sale in favour of the complainant.
He is not aware of the fact that who deposited the aforesaid cheque bearing No.030062 in his account.
Admittedly, the aforesaid cheque was returned to the bank and the amount was not deposited in the applicant's account.
The applicant is in custody since 31.05.2023.
His custodial interrogation or trial is not required in the matter.
Trial will take time for its conclusion.
Hence, prayer is made to enlarge the applicant on bail.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application on the ground that the cheque bearing No.030062 amounting to Rs.5,00,000/- was deposited in the account of applicant, which itself shows his involvement in the crime and allegations leveled against the applicant are serious in nature.
Hence, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

Having considered the rival submissions, material pointed out by learned counsel for the parties,
specially with regard to the fact that as per statement of the complainant recorded during investigation, the person who executed the agreement to sale was aged about 60 years and the fact that the cheque said to be deposited in the account of the applicant was returned to the bank, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting anything on the merits of the cas e, the application is allowed.
It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
This application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE bj/-
